title: GitHub - Tthanh2k6/turbo-browser-mcp: High-speed Playwright MCP server with multi-tab batching, compact delta DOM snapshots, React/Shadow DOM/iframe form filling, disk file uploads, and submit guards
excerpt: High-speed Playwright MCP server with multi-tab batching, compact delta DOM snapshots, React/Shadow DOM/iframe form filling, disk file uploads, and submit guards - Tthanh2k6/turbo-browser-mcp
content_html:
turbo-browser-mcp is a Playwright-based Model Context Protocol (MCP) server built to cut LLM token waste and multi-turn latency in browser automation. It consolidates 25-33 fine-grained browser primitives into 10 batched tools featuring delta DOM snapshots, single-turn React/Shadow DOM/iframe form prefill, direct disk file uploads (no Base64 in context), parallel tab sessions, network blocking presets, and a default human-in-the-loop Submit guard.

At-a-Glance Performance & Token Scorecard

All figures below come from benchmarks/benchmark.mjs (npm run benchmark) running headless Chromium locally with exact OpenAI o200k_base tokenization (tiktoken 0.14.0):

Note on latency vs LLM inference turns: Eliminating 10 round-trips on a 10-field form saves both 7x in browser execution (574 ms -> 82 ms) and 10 separate LLM inference round-trips (2-5s per turn in agent loops) plus ~71,800 replayed history tokens.

Why Browser Agents Stall: Side-by-Side Workflow

Standard MCP servers charge an LLM round-trip for every snapshot, field fill, <select> choice, upload, and verification check. Each turn re-sends the growing conversation history back into the model.

What turbo-browser-mcp Supports

1. Connection & Session Isolation

  • 4 connection modes (--mode auto|cdp|persistent|launch):
    • auto (default): probes --cdp http://127.0.0.1:9222 first so agents can reuse an existing signed-in browser session, then falls back to launching Chromium.
    • cdp: attach directly to a running Chromium/Chrome/Edge remote debugging port.
    • persistent: launch with a reusable --user-data-dir profile across runs.
    • launch: start a clean browser session (--headless by default, or --headed).
  • Auto binary discovery (src/playwright-loader.mjs): checks playwright-core cache revisions across Windows, macOS, and Linux, system installs of Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave, and Chromium, or an explicit --executable <path>.
  • Per-tab isolation (tabs_batch): open tabs inside named isolatedContext sandboxes with separate cookies and storage, batch-open up to 10 concurrent URLs (open_many), activate, reload, go back/forward, resize viewport, and emulate colorScheme, media, reducedMotion, contrast, forcedColors, or custom userAgent.

2. DOM, Iframe & Shadow DOM Inspection (inspect_compact)

  • Snapshot modes: interactive, forms, article, and all.
  • Cross-boundary traversal: flattens main frame DOM, child iframes (includeFrames, frameIdx), and open Shadow DOM. Injects an init script hooking Element.prototype.attachShadow (WeakMap + WeakRef/FinalizationRegistry + window.__tbmGetShadowRoot) to keep post-init closed Shadow roots inspectable and guarded, traverses <slot> assignedNodes({ flatten: true }), and supports Form-Associated Custom Elements.
  • Token controls: onlyChanged: true emits only elements added or changed since the prior snapshot; query filters by regex or substring; boxes: true adds [box=x,y,w,h] only when needed; maxChars caps payload size; savePath writes full output to disk.

3. Single-Turn Smart Form Engine (smart_fill_form)

Prefills an entire form in one MCP call while flushing microtasks and macrotasks between controlled inputs:

  • Standard & framework inputs: text, email, password, number, date, textarea, <input type="range">, checkboxes, radio groups (check, not, overwrite). Triggers React-controlled state updates via native property setters and synthetic events.
  • Selects & custom widgets: <select> and <select multiple> (option / values), ARIA comboboxes, ARIA switches, contenteditable rich editors, and Gmail compose dialogs (gmail: { to, subject, body }).
  • Frame & wildcard targeting: target specific iframes via frameIdx, or set all: true to populate matching controls across frames.
  • Direct disk uploads: pass file or files paths directly to Playwright setInputFiles without loading binary files or Base64 strings into LLM context.
  • Atomic verification: pass returnSnapshot: true to inspect the updated form state in the same tool response.

4. 16 Interactive Actions & Multi-Step Chaining (act_fast, batch_actions)

  • act_fast actions: click, dblclick, hover, focus, clear, fill, type (slowly, delayMs, submit), select, check, uncheck, drag, drop (file, files, or custom MIME dropData), press (key + modifiers: Alt, Control, ControlOrMeta, Meta, Shift), scroll (dx, dy), wait (ms, state, loadState, text, textGone, url), and upload.
  • Targeting options: compact [eN] ref, CSS selector, visible text, label, or viewport (x, y) coordinates, with button (left, right, middle) and frameIdx.
  • batch_actions: runs an ordered list of DOM actions and nested smart_fill_form steps in one MCP call, stopping safely if blocked by the Submit guard or optionally continuing on step errors (continueOnError).

5. Clean Extraction, Evaluation & Media Capture (extract_clean_text, evaluate_js, capture_page)

  • extract_clean_text: extracts readable plain text or compact Markdown (format: "text" | "markdown") from main/article containers and iframes, stripped of script and style noise.
  • evaluate_js: runs JS expressions or (el, arg) element functions in any frame (frameIdx) with JSON-serialized results and optional savePath export.
  • capture_page: full-page or element-scoped screenshots (png or jpeg with quality, css or device scale, optional returnImage) and PDF generation saved to a confined savePath.

6. Network Blocking, Storage State & Diagnostics (network_session, page_diagnostics)

  • network_session presets: turbo, no-images, no-media, and clean (unblock all), alongside custom blockResources and blockUrls patterns.
  • Session & storage management: read/write/clear browser cookies, localStorage/sessionStorage, and export or reload full Playwright storageState JSON files (saveStorageStatePath, loadStorageStatePath).
  • page_diagnostics: defaults to errors-only (level: "errors", statusFilter: "errors") to surface failures cleanly without flooding context, while supporting all, includeStatic, urlFilter, deep request/response inspection (reqId + part), completed downloads, and dialog auto-handling (dialogPolicy: accept/dismiss).

Reproducible Benchmarks (npm run benchmark)

Run the benchmark suite yourself with Chromium and Playwright installed:

npm run benchmark

Environment & methodology: Headless Chromium via playwright-core, counting exact OpenAI o200k_base tokens via Python tiktoken (approx-bpe fallback if tiktoken is unavailable). Cumulative workflow tokens model standard chat-history replay across $N$ sequential turns: $\sum_{i=1}^{N} (N - i + 1) \cdot T_i$, plus a one-shot baseline where the first turn captures context before acting.

Safety: Human-in-the-Loop Submit Guard & Path Confinement

  1. Human-in-the-loop Submit Guard (allowSubmit=false by default):
    • smart_fill_form (stopBeforeSubmit: true), act_fast, and batch_actions inspect matching elements, W3C AccName labels (isSafeSubmitter), implicit HTML form Enter submissions, key chords (Shift+Enter, Enter+Shift), HTMLFormElement.prototype.submit/requestSubmit, and same-origin iframe contentWindow/contentDocument proxies.
    • Final actions resembling Submit, Publish, Send, Post, Apply, Confirm, or payment triggers are blocked unless allowSubmit: true is explicitly passed or --allow-submit is enabled at startup.
    • Trade-off: pre-existing closed Shadow roots on already-open CDP tabs (attached before the init script ran) or strict cross-origin sandboxed frames fall back to Playwright frame handles, coordinate actions, and keyboard input.
  2. Workspace Path Confinement (TURBO_BROWSER_SAVE_ROOT):
    • File outputs (savePath, saveStorageStatePath) and state inputs (loadStorageStatePath) are strictly confined to the current working directory or TURBO_BROWSER_SAVE_ROOT.
    • Lexical checks, lstatSync/readlinkSync symlink verification, and realpathSync validation block .. traversal, UNC network paths, dangling symlinks, cyclic symlinks, and Windows junctions before reading or writing.

Commit safety added in v0.5.0 (from Show HN and dev.to feedback)

Readers who run agents on real portals pointed out three gaps in a label-based guard. v0.5.0 adds an opt-in answer to each. expect, submissionKey and allowDuplicate appear in the batch_actions schema; act_fast accepts the same arguments without advertising them. The network guard is turned on with TURBO_BROWSER_NETWORK_GUARD=true and covers act_fast, batch_actions and smart_fill_form.

  1. A landed click is not a confirmed submission → expect. After an allowed submit, pass expect: { urlMatches?, textMatches?, selector?, timeoutMs? }. The result carries submitVerified and evidence (the new URL, a text snippet such as a receipt number, or the matched selector). If nothing shows up in time you get submitVerified: false and a reason, so the agent does not report "done" on an empty submission list.
  2. A re-run is a second entry, not a retry → submissionKey. With submissionKey: "portal:2026-11-15:entry-42", every allowed submit is appended to a JSONL ledger (~/.turbo-browser-mcp/submissions.jsonl, or TURBO_BROWSER_LEDGER, or ledgerPath inside the save root). A later call with the same key is refused with blockedBy: "ledger" unless allowDuplicate: true.
  3. Labels lie → modal rule + networkGuard. On many Korean portals the last step reads 다음 and the real commit is a 확인 inside a modal that opens afterwards.
    • Affirmative buttons (확인, OK, Yes, Confirm, 確認, 确定, Đồng ý, …) inside dialog / [role=dialog] / [role=alertdialog] / [aria-modal=true] now count as commits (blockedBy: "modal"). Cookie banners (dialog text mentions cookies) and date/time pickers (dialog contains a calendar grid or date input) are excluded; a confirmation that only mentions "privacy" or "consent" is still blocked.
    • When an action makes the page call form.submit() / requestSubmit() or fire a submit event and the guard stops it, the result now says so (submitSuppressed, note) instead of a bare ok: true. The action itself (a select, a check) still counts as done, so batches continue.
    • Common Korean, Japanese, Chinese and Vietnamese submit labels were added (제출, 신청, 등록, 결제, 送信, 確定, 提交, Hoàn tất, …), and 다음, 次へ, 下一步 are treated like Next.
    • TURBO_BROWSER_NETWORK_GUARD=true is the safety net that does not depend on labels: while submitting is not allowed, non-GET navigations and same-site fetch/XHR POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE are stopped and reported (blockedBy: "network", networkBlocked[]). Blocked navigations get a 204 so the page and the half-filled form stay put. Let harmless endpoints through with TURBO_BROWSER_NETWORK_GUARD_ALLOW="/autosave$,/analytics". Per call, the undeclared arguments networkGuard, networkGuardAllow and networkGuardSettleMs override the env values. It is off by default because multi-step wizards often POST on every "Next".
    • Every blocked result now says which mechanism stopped it: blockedBy is label, modal, network or ledger.

Limits:

  • The network guard watches the action plus networkGuardSettleMs (250 ms) afterwards, so a commit fired later by a timer is not caught. WebSocket messages, requests made by a service worker, and cross-site fetch POSTs are not inspected (cross-site navigations are). Patterns in TURBO_BROWSER_NETWORK_GUARD_ALLOW are split on commas, so a pattern cannot contain one.
  • The ledger is written only when the call returns. If the call throws after the page already sent the submission (for example a navigation timeout), nothing is recorded; check the site before re-running.
  • expect.selector that is not a valid selector never matches, so the call reports submitVerified: false after the timeout.

Human-first sessions (wait_for_human, --open-profile)

Some sites fail their bot check whenever the browser is remote-controlled, so a person has to open the same profile in a normal browser first. turbo-browser-mcp does not try to hide automation: no stealth plugins, no fingerprint or navigator.webdriver patching, no CAPTCHA solving. It supports two hand-off flows instead.

  1. Before the session: turbo-browser-mcp --open-profile --url https://site.example/login opens plain Chrome (no debugging port, no automation flags) on the dedicated profile ~/.turbo-browser-mcp/chrome-profile (or --user-data-dir). The human logs in or passes the check and closes the window. Then start the server with --user-data-dir <same path> or --launch-chrome, and the agent reuses those cookies. This works for sites that check at login; a site that re-checks on every request will still see an automated browser.
  2. During the session: the agent calls wait_for_human with a message and a condition (urlMatches, selector, textMatches or textGone). The tool brings the tab to the front and polls until the condition holds, then the agent continues in the same tab with the same cookies. Keep timeoutMs below your MCP client's request timeout and call it again to keep waiting.
{
  "name": "wait_for_human",
  "arguments": {
    "message": "Please sign in and finish the security check, then leave the tab open.",
    "selector": "#account-menu",
    "timeoutMs": 120000
  }
}

Quick Start

Install & Check Environment

git clone https://github.com/Tthanh2k6/turbo-browser-mcp.git
cd turbo-browser-mcp
npm install
npm run doctor

If you need Playwright's bundled Chromium (or have no system Chrome/Edge/Brave installed):

npx playwright-core install chromium

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "turbo-browser": {
      "command": "node",

      "env": {

      }
    }
  }

  "mcpServers": {

      "command": "npx",

Unattended Overnight / AFK Automation (Eliminating Chrome 144+ Approval Prompts)

In Chrome 136+/144+, enabling chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging on the default User Data directory exposes a WebSocket in DevToolsActivePort that displays an "Allow remote debugging?" prompt whenever a new WebSocket client connects. turbo-browser-mcp provides two built-in solutions so overnight AFK multi-agent runs never hang on a prompt:

  1. Automatic CDP Keep-Alive Bridge Daemon (npm run bridge / --bridge, enabled automatically on DevToolsActivePort):
    • Spawns a detached background multiplexer (src/cdp-bridge.mjs on http://127.0.0.1:9224) that holds one persistent upstream WebSocket to Chrome open indefinitely and intercepts Browser.close so downstream scripts never terminate your browser.
    • You click Allow once when starting your session; afterwards, any number of MCP servers, CLI scripts, or subagents can connect and disconnect all night with 0 additional prompts.
  2. Zero-Prompt Dedicated Profile Launcher (npm run launch-chrome / --launch-chrome):
    • Launches Chrome with --remote-debugging-port=9222 and a dedicated --user-data-dir (~/.turbo-browser-mcp/chrome-profile), where Chrome exposes standard HTTP/WS CDP with 0 confirmation dialogs even on the very first connection.

Connection & Session Isolation 4 connection modes (--mode auto|cdp|persistent|launch): auto (default): probes --cdp http://127.0.0.1:9222 first so agents can reuse an existing signed-in browser session, then falls back to launching Chromium. cdp: attach directly to a running Chromium/Chrome/Edge remote debugging port. persistent: launch with a reusable --user-data-dir profile across runs. launch: start a clean browser session (--headless by default, or --headed). Auto binary discovery (src/playwright-loader.mjs): checks playwright-core cache revisions across Windows, macOS, and Linux, system installs of Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave, and Chromium, or an explicit --executable <path>. Per-tab isolation (tabs_batch): open tabs inside named isolatedContext sandboxes with separate cookies and storage, batch-open up to 10 concurrent URLs (open_many), activate, reload, go back/forward, resize viewport, and emulate colorScheme, media, reducedMotion, contrast, forcedColors, or custom userAgent. 2. DOM, Iframe & Shadow DOM Inspection (inspect_compact) Snapshot modes: interactive, forms, article, and all. Cross-boundary traversal: flattens main frame DOM, child iframes (includeFrames, frameIdx), and open Shadow DOM. Injects an init script hooking Element.prototype.attachShadow (WeakMap + WeakRef/FinalizationRegistry + window.__tbmGetShadowRoot) to keep post-init closed Shadow roots inspectable and guarded, traverses <slot> assignedNodes({ flatten: true }), and supports Form-Associated Custom Elements. Token controls: onlyChanged: true emits only elements added or changed since the prior snapshot; query filters by regex or substring; boxes: true adds [box=x,y,w,h] only when needed; maxChars caps payload size; savePath writes full output to disk. 3. Single-Turn Smart Form Engine (smart_fill_form) Prefills an entire form in one MCP call while flushing microtasks and macrotasks between controlled inputs: Standard & framework inputs: text, email, password, number, date, textarea, <input type="range">, checkboxes, radio groups (check, not, overwrite). Triggers React-controlled state updates via native property setters and synthetic events. Selects & custom widgets: <select> and <select multiple> (option / values), ARIA comboboxes, ARIA switches, contenteditable rich editors, and Gmail compose dialogs (gmail: { to, subject, body }). Frame & wildcard targeting: target specific iframes via frameIdx, or set all: true to populate matching controls across frames. Direct disk uploads: pass file or files paths directly to Playwright setInputFiles without loading binary files or Base64 strings into LLM context. Atomic verification: pass returnSnapshot: true to inspect the updated form state in the same tool response. 4. 16 Interactive Actions & Multi-Step Chaining (act_fast, batch_actions) act_fast actions: click, dblclick, hover, focus, clear, fill, type (slowly, delayMs, submit), select, check, uncheck, drag, drop (file, files, or custom MIME dropData), press (key + modifiers: Alt, Control, ControlOrMeta, Meta, Shift), scroll (dx, dy), wait (ms, state, loadState, text, textGone, url), and upload. Targeting options: compact [eN] ref, CSS selector, visible text, label, or viewport (x, y) coordinates, with button (left, right, middle) and frameIdx. batch_actions: runs an ordered list of DOM actions and nested smart_fill_form steps in one MCP call, stopping safely if blocked by the Submit guard or optionally continuing on step errors (continueOnError). 5. Clean Extraction, Evaluation & Media Capture (extract_clean_text, evaluate_js, capture_page) extract_clean_text: extracts readable plain text or compact Markdown (format: "text" | "markdown") from main/article containers and iframes, stripped of script and style noise. evaluate_js: runs JS expressions or (el, arg) element functions in any frame (frameIdx) with JSON-serialized results and optional savePath export. capture_page: full-page or element-scoped screenshots (png or jpeg with quality, css or device scale, optional returnImage) and PDF generation saved to a confined savePath. 6. Network Blocking, Storage State & Diagnostics (network_session, page_diagnostics) network_session presets: turbo, no-images, no-media, and clean (unblock all), alongside custom blockResources and blockUrls patterns. Session & storage management: read/write/clear browser cookies, localStorage/sessionStorage, and export or reload full Playwright storageState JSON files (saveStorageStatePath, loadStorageStatePath). page_diagnostics: defaults to errors-only (level: "errors", statusFilter: "errors") to surface failures cleanly without flooding context, while supporting all, includeStatic, urlFilter, deep request/response inspection (reqId + part), completed downloads, and dialog auto-handling (dialogPolicy: accept/dismiss). Cumulative workflow tokens model standard chat-history replay across $N$ sequential turns: $\sum_{i=1}^{N} (N - i + 1) \cdot T_i$, plus a one-shot baseline where the first turn captures context before acting. 1. Final actions resembling Submit, Publish, Send, Post, Apply, Confirm, or payment triggers are blocked unless allowSubmit: true is explicitly passed or --allow-submit is enabled at startup. Trade-off: pre-existing closed Shadow roots on already-open CDP tabs (attached before the init script ran) or strict cross-origin sandboxed frames fall back to Playwright frame handles, coordinate actions, and keyboard input. Workspace Path Confinement (TURBO_BROWSER_SAVE_ROOT): File outputs (savePath, saveStorageStatePath) and state inputs (loadStorageStatePath) are strictly confined to the current working directory or TURBO_BROWSER_SAVE_ROOT. Lexical checks, lstatSync/readlinkSync symlink verification, and realpathSync validation block .. traversal, UNC network paths, dangling symlinks, cyclic symlinks, and Windows junctions before reading or writing. Commit safety added in v0.5.0 (from Show HN and dev.to feedback) Readers who run agents on real portals pointed out three gaps in a label-based guard. v0.5.0 adds an opt-in answer to each. expect, submissionKey and allowDuplicate appear in the batch_actions schema; act_fast accepts the same arguments without advertising them. The network guard is turned on with TURBO_BROWSER_NETWORK_GUARD=true and covers act_fast, batch_actions and smart_fill_form. A landed click is not a confirmed submission → expect. After an allowed submit, pass expect: { urlMatches?, textMatches?, selector?, timeoutMs? }. The result carries submitVerified and evidence (the new URL, a text snippet such as a receipt number, or the matched selector). If nothing shows up in time you get submitVerified: false and a reason, so the agent does not report "done" on an empty submission list. A re-run is a second entry, not a retry → submissionKey. With submissionKey: "portal:2026-11-15:entry-42", every allowed submit is appended to a JSONL ledger (~/.turbo-browser-mcp/submissions.jsonl, or TURBO_BROWSER_LEDGER, or ledgerPath inside the save root). A later call with the same key is refused with blockedBy: "ledger" unless allowDuplicate: true. Labels lie → modal rule + networkGuard. On many Korean portals the last step reads 다음 and the real commit is a 확인 inside a modal that opens afterwards. Affirmative buttons (확인, OK, Yes, Confirm, 確認, 确定, Đồng ý, …) inside dialog / [role=dialog] / [role=alertdialog] / [aria-modal=true] now count as commits (blockedBy: "modal"). Cookie banners (dialog text mentions cookies) and date/time pickers (dialog contains a calendar grid or date input) are excluded; a confirmation that only mentions "privacy" or "consent" is still blocked. When an action makes the page call form.submit() / requestSubmit() or fire a submit event and the guard stops it, the result now says so (submitSuppressed, note) instead of a bare ok: true. The action itself (a select, a check) still counts as done, so batches continue. Common Korean, Japanese, Chinese and Vietnamese submit labels were added (제출, 신청, 등록, 결제, 送信, 確定, 提交, Hoàn tất, …), and 다음, 次へ, 下一步 are treated like Next. TURBO_BROWSER_NETWORK_GUARD=true is the safety net that does not depend on labels: while submitting is not allowed, non-GET navigations and same-site fetch/XHR POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE are stopped and reported (blockedBy: "network", networkBlocked[]). Blocked navigations get a 204 so the page and the half-filled form stay put. Let harmless endpoints through with TURBO_BROWSER_NETWORK_GUARD_ALLOW="/autosave$,/analytics". Per call, the undeclared arguments networkGuard, networkGuardAllow and networkGuardSettleMs override the env values. It is off by default because multi-step wizards often POST on every "Next". Every blocked result now says which mechanism stopped it: blockedBy is label, modal, network or ledger. Limits: The network guard watches the action plus networkGuardSettleMs (250 ms) afterwards, so a commit fired later by a timer is not caught. WebSocket messages, requests made by a service worker, and cross-site fetch POSTs are not inspected (cross-site navigations are). Patterns in TURBO_BROWSER_NETWORK_GUARD_ALLOW are split on commas, so a pattern cannot contain one. The ledger is written only when the call returns. If the call throws after the page already sent the submission (for example a navigation timeout), nothing is recorded; check the site before re-running. expect.selector that is not a valid selector never matches, so the call reports submitVerified: false after the timeout. Human-first sessions (wait_for_human, --open-profile) Some sites fail their bot check whenever the browser is remote-controlled, so a person has to open the same profile in a normal browser first. turbo-browser-mcp does not try to hide automation: no stealth plugins, no fingerprint or navigator.webdriver patching, no CAPTCHA solving. It supports two hand-off flows instead. Before the session: turbo-browser-mcp --open-profile --url https://site.example/login opens plain Chrome (no debugging port, no automation flags) on the dedicated profile ~/.turbo-browser-mcp/chrome-profile (or --user-data-dir). The human logs in or passes the check and closes the window. Then start the server with --user-data-dir <same path> or --launch-chrome, and the agent reuses those cookies. This works for sites that check at login; a site that re-checks on every request will still see an automated browser. During the session: the agent calls wait_for_human with a message and a condition (urlMatches, selector, textMatches or textGone). The tool brings the tab to the front and polls until the condition holds, then the agent continues in the same tab with the same cookies. Keep timeoutMs below your MCP client's request timeout and call it again to keep waiting. { "name": "wait_for_human", "arguments": { "message": "Please sign in and finish the security check, then
